text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of working on a huge project all at once, teams use an iterative development process. They break the work into small, manageable time periods called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. At the start of a sprint, the team selects tasks from a prioritized list called the backlog. These tasks are often described as user stories, which simply explain a feature from the end user's perspective. To keep everyone on track, the team holds short daily meetings called standups, where each member reports what they did yesterday and what they plan to do today. This continuous cycle allows for quick adjustments and ensures the final product meets real user needs.
